title: Is It Hidden Inside
statement:
A text `s` is a **subsequence** of a text `t` if you can get `s` by deleting zero or more letters of `t` without changing the order of the remaining letters (`ace` is a subsequence of `abcde`, `aec` is not).

Return `true` if `s` is a subsequence of `t`, otherwise `false`. The empty text is a subsequence of every text.
constraints: s and t contain lowercase letters

examples.explanation: Keep a, c and e of abcde.
After the e there is no c left.

hints.nudge: Walk through t once. What do you need to remember about s while you do?
hints.pattern: Two pointers: one in s (the next letter still to be found) and one running through t; advance the pointer in s whenever the letters match.
hints.walkthrough: Match the letters of s greedily from the left: take the earliest occurrence in t of s[0], then the earliest occurrence of s[1] after it, and so on. Taking the earliest possible match never hurts, because it leaves the most letters of t for the rest. So a single pointer `i` into s is enough: scan t, and each time the current letter of t equals s[i], move i forward. At the end s is a subsequence exactly when i reached the end of s. O(len(s) + len(t)).
